**What I did**
- I set a `width` parameter to 80.
- I sketched the 80 × 50 mm rectangle on XY with one corner at the origin. Width is driven by `width` and depth is fixed at 50.
- In the same sketch I added four Ø5 mm circles, each dimensioned 8 mm in from both edges of its corner. I also added a Ø12 mm circle at `width/2`, 25 mm, which is the middle of the plate.
- I extruded the outer profile 5 mm (Z 0 to 5), and the circles became holes.
- I exported `/lab/out/plate-80.stl`.
- I set `width` to 60, which regenerated the model. I exported `/lab/out/plate-60.stl`.

**Checks**
- **80 mm plate:** the bounding box is 80 × 50 × 5. The volume is 19,041.9 mm³, which matches 20,000 − 305π.
- **60 mm plate:** the bounding box is 60 × 50 × 5. The volume is 14,041.9 mm³, which matches 15,000 − 305π. The centre of mass is at X = 30, so the holes are symmetric. Both plates have 5 cylindrical faces.
- I didn't open the STL files after exporting. I only checked the model they came from.

**Problems along the way**
- My first two tool calls were mistakes with made-up command names. They failed and changed nothing.
- My first attempt used a rectangle with hard-coded dimensions. I undid it so the width would be parametric.
- A circle centre given as an expression (`"width-8"`) was rejected. I used dimension constraints instead.
- The default extrude ignored the circles, giving a solid 20,0
